identity.title: Nucleic acid amplification-free, aptamer-gated Cas13a-Csm6 cascade for signal-on electrochemical detection of carcinoembryonic antigen in esophageal cancer.

content.abstract: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) is a clinically relevant tumor-associated biomarker that has been investigated for auxiliary assessment and monitoring in the context of esophageal cancer. However, conventional CEA assays often require antibodies, complicated procedures, or nucleic acid amplification strategies to achieve high sensitivity. Herein, we developed a nucleic acid amplification-free, aptamer-gated Cas13a-Csm6 cascade electrochemical aptasensor for sensitive CEA analysis. In the proposed sensing model, the CEA aptamer serves as both a target recognition element and a Cas13a activator. In the absence of CEA, the free aptamer activates Cas13a, triggering cleavage of the Csm6 activator precursor and generation of secondary activators for Csm6. The activated Csm6 subsequently cleaves methylene blue (MB)-labeled single-stranded RNA reporters immobilized on the electrode surface, resulting in MB release and a decreased electrochemical signal. The increased signal observed in the presence of CEA is consistent with the proposed model that CEA binding may reduce the availability or accessibility of the aptamer for Cas13a activation, thereby attenuating the downstream Cas13a-Csm6 cascade. The proposed method achieved a detection limit of 1.12 pg/mL, which was approximately 21-fold lower than that of the Cas13a-only system (23.5 pg/mL). Without requiring PCR, RPA, RCA, or other nucleic acid amplification procedures, the platform exhibited excellent selectivity against interfering proteins and reliable performance in 1% fetal bovine serum. This work provides a sensitive nucleic acid amplification-free CRISPR-assisted electrochemical strategy for CEA quantification and highlights the potential of Cas13a-Csm6 cascades for tumor-associated biomarker analysis.
